chapter.title: When a station jams

cards.body: Your line ran 40 times yesterday and one run failed. Which station dropped the item? By default, n8n keeps a record of each trip down the belt, and the station that jammed shows up in red. **When one station jams, you find that station and fix it. You don't rebuild the line.**
cards.simpler: Your line ran 40 times yesterday, and one run failed. Which station dropped the item? By default, n8n keeps a record of each trip down the belt. The station that jammed shows up in red. **When one station jams, you find it and fix just that one.** You don't rebuild the whole line. It's like a flat tire: you change the tire, not the car.

cards.prompt: Your form-to-Slack line ran 40 times yesterday. This morning, run 23 shows an error. What's your first move?

options.text: Delete the workflow and build it again, carefully this time
Open run 23 in the Executions list and look for the red node
Run the workflow again with a fresh test form

whyNot.a: That's rebuilding the whole line, not finding the jam: 39 runs worked, so most of it is fine.
whyNot.c: That's a new item on the belt, not the one that jammed: it may go through fine and hide the problem.

cards.reteach: With its usual settings, n8n saves your runs, including the broken ones. The failed run shows exactly which station stopped and what it was holding. So you start there, not with a rebuild.

cards.title: Each trip is recorded
cards.body:
With its usual settings, n8n saves each run of your workflow as an *execution*, a record of one trip down the belt. The Executions list shows them, each with a time and a status: succeeded or error.

Open a failed one and you see your line frozen at the moment it jammed. **The node that failed is marked in red.** Click it to see the error message, n8n's note on what went wrong, plus the item it was holding.

It's like a plane's black box, minus the drama. It recorded the trip, so you don't have to guess.
cards.simpler: Usually, each time your workflow runs, n8n saves a record of that one trip down the belt, called an *execution*. The Executions list shows them, with the time and whether each worked or hit an error. Open a failed one and you see your line stopped where it jammed. **The failed station, called a node, is marked in red.** Click it to see what went wrong and the item it held. It's like a plane's black box.

cards.title: Priya's lead line
cards.body: Priya's workflow takes a new website form, adds a row to Google Sheets, then posts in Slack. On Tuesday at 9:12, run 14 failed. In the Executions list the Slack node was red, with the message *channel_not_found*. Her Slack node had the channel typed in by name, #sales-leads, and someone had renamed it #leads over the weekend. Nobody told the robot. She picked #leads from the list in the Slack node, retried run 14 with the saved workflow, and the message landed. That took two minutes, with no rebuild.
cards.simpler: Priya's workflow takes a new website form, adds a row to Google Sheets, then posts in Slack. On Tuesday at 9:12, run 14 failed. In Executions, the Slack station was red with the note *channel_not_found*. Her Slack station had the channel name typed in: #sales-leads. Over the weekend, someone renamed that channel to #leads. Nobody told the robot. Priya picked #leads from the list in the Slack station and retried run 14 using her saved fix. The message landed. **Two minutes, no rebuild.**

cards.prompt: Your Google Sheets node has the sheet name typed in: 'Leads 2026'. Now it's red, and the error says it can't find that sheet. A colleague renamed it 'Leads' yesterday. What do you do?

options.text: Retry the failed run as it is, a few times
Point the Sheets node at 'Leads', then retry the failed run
Rebuild every node from the form onwards

whyNot.a: That's repeating the jam, not fixing it: nothing changed, so it fails the same way.
whyNot.c: That's rebuilding the line, not fixing the station: the form and the other nodes did their jobs.

cards.reteach: The red node tells you which station broke and why. Change that one station so the reason goes away (here, the sheet name), then send the same failed item through again.

cards.title: Hiccups versus real faults
cards.body:
Not every jam needs you. Sometimes an app is just slow for a second, like a door that sticks once. For that, open the node's Settings and switch on *Retry On Fail*, which makes n8n try that station again a few times before giving up.

Retry won't fix a wrong channel or a missing field. **A real fault fails the same way every time**, so retry just jams three times instead of once.

To hear about jams without checking, give the workflow an *error workflow*: a second small line that starts with an Error Trigger node and messages you when the main one fails.
cards.simpler: Sometimes an app is slow for a second, like a door that sticks once. For that, turn on *Retry On Fail* in the station's Settings, so n8n tries again a few times. Retry can't fix a wrong channel or a missing field. **A real fault fails the same way every time.** To hear about jams, add an *error workflow*: a small second line, starting with an Error Trigger node, that messages you when the main one fails.

cards.body: Sam's Gmail node went red: no address to send to. He rebuilt that node three times, and it kept failing. The real fault was one station back, in an Edit Fields node that copies the form's 'Email' answer into a field called 'to' for Gmail. The form question had been renamed to 'Work email', so Edit Fields found no 'Email' and handed Gmail an empty 'to'. **Click the red node and read its input first**: if the item arrived broken, the fix belongs upstream, in an earlier station.
cards.simpler: Sam's Gmail station went red: it had no address to send to. He rebuilt that station three times, and it still failed. The real problem was one station earlier. There, an Edit Fields station copied the form's 'Email' answer into a field called 'to', for Gmail to use. But the form question had been renamed to 'Work email'. So Edit Fields found no 'Email', and Gmail got an empty 'to'. **Click the red station and read what it was handed first.** If the item arrived broken, fix the station before it.

cards.prompt: Run 52 failed. The Gmail node is red with 'no recipient', and its input shows the email field arrived empty. Where does the fix go?

options.text: In the Gmail node: rewrite it until it works
One station earlier, where the email field should get filled
In the Gmail node's Settings: switch on Retry On Fail

whyNot.a: That's the station that showed the jam, not the one that caused it: Gmail can't send to an empty address.
whyNot.c: That's the fix for a hiccup, not a real fault: an empty field stays empty on every try.

cards.reteach: Red marks where the line stopped, not always why. Check what the red node was handed. If the item arrived broken, walk back one station and fix it there.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: When a run fails, open it in Executions, click the red node, and read both the error and what it was handed. **Fix that one station, or the one before it, then retry the same run.** Save Retry On Fail for apps that hiccup.
cards.simpler: When a run fails, open it in Executions and click the red station. Read the error, and read what the station was handed. **Fix that one station, or the one before it, then retry the same run.** Keep Retry On Fail for apps that sometimes get stuck for a moment.

cards.body:
Open n8n, click Executions, and open your last run. Click each node and look at what went in and what came out. Then open one node's Settings and find Retry On Fail.

Tomorrow: one switch, and your line runs while you're asleep.
cards.simpler: Open n8n, click Executions, and open your last run. Click each station, one at a time. For each one, **look at what went in and what came out**. It's like peeking inside each box on the belt. Then open one station's Settings and find the switch called Retry On Fail. Tomorrow: one switch, and your line runs while you sleep.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now find which node failed, read why, and fix it without rebuilding the workflow.

dubious_claims: Renaming a Slack channel keeps its ID, and n8n's Slack node usually stores the ID when you pick a channel from the list, so renaming #sales-leads to #leads would only cause channel_not_found if the channel was typed in by name.
Same issue with the Google Sheets rename: picking a sheet from the list stores its ID, so renaming 'Leads 2026' to 'Leads' only breaks a node that was set up by name.
The open loop 'your line runs while you're asleep' clashes with card 1, where the line already ran 40 times overnight; also the chapter ends on the 'try' card, not on that line.
'n8n saves every run' depends on the save settings and how long the plan keeps records; it's true by default but not guaranteed.
repairedFrom.why: Sam's 'fix it upstream' lesson doesn't hold up: if the form question changed from 'Email' to 'Work email', the item arrived carrying the address under the new name, and the quickest fix is changing the field name inside the Gmail node, so the card teaches the opposite of what really happens.
repairedFrom.fix: Add a real station in between, e.g. an Edit Fields node that copies 'Email' into 'to', so the empty field is clearly made one station back and the fix clearly belongs there.
